text: Costco sells you a hot dog and a drink for $1.50.
Adjust for inflation and it'd be around $4.50 today.
The story goes, the founder told his successor,
raise the hot dog and I'll kill you.
Because the hot dog isn't the product, you are.
It's a loss leader, a deal so cheap it pulls you into the store.
Last year, Costco sold over 245 million of those combos, but to get in, you need a membership.
In its latest year, Costco made about $5.9 billion from fees alone.
That's roughly two-thirds of its whole profit.
That's the Mirage. The cheap hot dog isn't losing money. It's selling the membership.
So when a deal looks too good, ask what it's really selling you.
